reason: The cited evidence does not address the key premises. E1 discusses corrosion in Mg-Zn, Mg-Ti, Zn-Ti alloys but not the proposed metastable-to-equilibrium evolution or its effect on oxide scales in Mg-containing lightweight HEAs. E2 concerns a Cantor alloy (CoCrFeMnNi) processed by SPS, which remains single-phase FCC with no intermetallics, and does not involve Mg, lightweight compositions, or corrosion/oxidation behavior. Thus, no specific prior evidence supports the premises.
premises: Mechanical alloying produces a metastable solid solution with minor transient intermetallics
Controlled heat treatment drives the metastable structure toward equilibrium fine intermetallics
Equilibrium intermetallics alter elemental partitioning and microsegregation
Altered partitioning promotes protective oxide scales (MgO/Al2O3) and enhances passivation
This improves corrosion and high-temperature oxidation over the as-alloyed baseline
